problem: Object-level topological navigation (RoboHop) gives sub-goal masks but its purely topological 'segment servoing' controller ignores traversability and obstacles, while learned controllers (PixNav, GNM) need training and generalize poorly.
motivation: Object-level topological maps are open-set, queryable and viewpoint-invariant, but bridging them to safe local motion without 3D maps or learned controllers is unsolved. The authors want a zero-shot, RGB-only, modular pipeline built on foundation models that avoids obstacles even when they were absent in the teach run.
key_idea: Combine RoboHop's topological object sub-goal planner with a local metric planner that builds a BEV traversability map from CLIP+SAM traversable segments and Depth Anything monocular depth, plus an automatic fallback to segment servoing.
insight: Ablation shows perception (segmentation + matching) is the bottleneck: replacing sim perception with FastSAM+LightGlue drops success by about 18 points (65.69 to 47.95), while predicted depth/traversability costs only about 5 more (to 43.14). Auto-switching to segment servoing when traversability is unreliable adds 11.64 points (62.14 to 73.78). Object-level graph connectivity also lets the robot reach seen-but-unvisited goals at comparable success.
method: Object-level topological map: SAM/FastSAM segments are nodes; intra-image Delaunay edges (weight 1) and inter-image edges (weight 0) from SuperPoint+LightGlue segment matching.
Localisation and global planning: current image matched to a temporal window of map images; Dijkstra gives a sub-goal cost mask over current-view segments.
BEV traversability: CLIP text queries (floor, ground, rug) classify each SAM segment as traversable; Depth-Anything projects traversable pixels and the sub-goal segment to a metric BEV map.
Sub-goal selection: the lowest-cost segment is the sub-goal; the farthest projected point inside it becomes the local metric goal.
Trajectory planning: distance-transform cost map from traversable mask edges, box-filtered; Dijkstra path; proportional line-following yaw control with fixed linear velocity.
Auto-switch control: when no reliable traversable region is visible, fall back to RoboHop segment servoing (softmax-weighted pixel offset to yaw, tau=5, gain 0.4) until traversability returns.

setting.backbone: Frozen foundation models: FastSAM/SAM, CLIP, Depth Anything, SuperPoint+LightGlue (no trained controller)
setting.action_space: continuous yaw control with fixed linear velocity
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D InstanceImageNav val scenes) plus real-world tests
setting.privileged: Teach (mapping) traverse from simulator path finder available to all methods; GT-Metric and GT-Topological variants use simulator instance masks, depth and navmesh, while the No-GT setting uses none.

numbers.eval_set_note: 36 environments x 3 episodes = 108 episodes, sampled from the InstanceImageNav validation set; 'Full' start distance 8-10m
numbers.extra: Map from simulator teach traverse; success radius 1m, 500 steps; the 'Full' distance range.

numbers.backbone: Simulator GT masks/depth/navmesh for goal masks and control
numbers.extra: Ground-truth goal masks (upper bound); privileged information

numbers.backbone: Simulator instance masks with topological map
numbers.extra: GT perception/localisation, simulator depth and traversability; privileged information

numbers_note: Success rate only. Tables give varying start-distance splits (easy/hard/full) rather than the official IIN metrics. Other variants are Alt Goals (Hard 50.54, Full 25.84) and the auto-switch ablation (250 steps, 62.14 vs 73.78).
results: In the No-GT setting TANGO reaches 61.76/43.14/21.57 SR (easy/hard/full), beating RoboHop (43.56/34.56/13.73) and the learned PixNav (51.96/39.22/14.0). The advantage holds with GT goal masks (GT-Metric hard 90.20 vs RoboHop 78.43). TANGO also reaches seen-but-unvisited goals at comparable success and runs in the real world at 5 Hz.
limitations: Perception errors (segment matching to the map) are the main failure cause; absolute No-GT success is low, especially on long trajectories (21.57%).
Purely topological edges cannot geometrically disambiguate sub-goals in the current view.
Text/segmentation-based traversability is error-prone, requiring the fallback controller; evaluation is on a small 108-episode subset.
